findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, unrelated to the annotation fix
findings.body: The ticker interval for the whole cleanup service was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This is not mentioned in the PR description and has nothing to do with the annotation deadlock. Every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, query history, temp files, annotations) now runs ten times as often. That is a production behaviour change that looks like a leftover debugging edit and should be reverted or justified separately.

findings.title: Routine per-batch cleanup progress is logged at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: The new fetch/delete loops log every batch with r.log.Error, both before and after the delete (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). These are normal informational messages, and on a healthy system they fire on every batch, even when err is nil. Each message also includes the full `ids` slice, which can hold up to the batch size (up to 32767 IDs). This floods error logs and makes real errors hard to find. The messages should be Debug or Info, the ID list should be dropped or truncated, and the `err` field should only be logged when there is an error.

findings.title: Quadratic string building of IDs for SQLite large-batch delete
findings.body: In deleteByIDs, the SQLite branch builds the IN list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. Each iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so building a list of N IDs costs O(N^2) bytes. With batch sizes up to 32767 (as exercised by the new 40003-annotation test), this produces hundreds of megabytes of intermediate copies per batch. Use a strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt to build the list in linear time.
